stemMd:
The table shows the net of a cube, seen from the side on which the letters P to U are printed; blank cells are not part of the net. The net is folded into a closed cube with **the letters on the outside**.

The cube is then placed on a table with face R resting on the table and face S facing an observer.

Which face of the cube is on the observer's right?

options.label: C
options.textMd: It cannot be determined from the information given

distractorRationale.b: P is opposite S, so with S facing the observer, P is at the back of the cube, not on the right.
distractorRationale.a: Q is on the observer's left. Choosing it means producing the mirror image of the cube, which happens if the net is folded with the letters inside, or if left and right are swapped while turning the cube.
distractorRationale.e: U is opposite R, so with R resting on the table, U is on top of the cube, not on the right.
distractorRationale.c: Once two neighbouring faces are fixed, one underneath and one at the front, the cube cannot turn any further, and the net with its letters outside fixes how the other faces are arranged. So the face on the right is determined.

accessibilityText: A spatial question posed through a table, with no drawing. The table is the net of a cube, seen from the printed side, on a grid of three rows and four columns, shaped like a staircase. Row 1: P in Column 1 and Q in Column 2. Row 2: R in Column 2, directly below Q, and S in Column 3, to the right of R. Row 3: T in Column 3, directly below S, and U in Column 4, to the right of T. The other cells are blank. The net is folded into a cube with the letters outside, and the cube is placed with face R on the table and face S facing an observer. The question asks which face is on the observer's right. The choices are face Q, face P, the statement that it cannot be determined from the information given, face T and face U.

provenance.notes: Original item. A folding script tracked each face's outward normal and in-plane directions with the printed side outward (and checked that every face frame stays right-handed), then found the face whose normal is the cross product of the front and bottom normals: T. The result was re-derived by hand with the two rotations given in the explanation.

review.author: wave6-polito-til-a-drawing-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Folding with the letters outside gives these opposite pairs: R and U, Q and T, S and P. Seen from outside, the faces around R run clockwise Q, S, T, P. With R on the table and seen from above, that order becomes anticlockwise. Putting S towards an observer in the south places T to the east, which is the observer's right. A check with coordinates (R +z, S +x, Q +y, T -y) gives Q on the left and T on the right. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-logic-drawing-run1) reached the same answer: I folded the net in 3D coordinates with the letters outside. With R on top, S is east, Q north, T south, P west and U at the bottom. Turning the cube over so that R rests on the table puts T on the north side, and an observer facing S from the east then has T on the right. I checked this a second way, folding with the letters face-down, and also got T. Opposite pairs are S-P, T-Q and R-U, and fixing the bottom and front faces leaves only one orientation, so C does not hold. Q is the answer you get from the mirror (letters-inside) fold.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: with the letters outside, the folded cube is fixed up to rotation, and fixing two adjacent faces fixes the rotation, so exactly one face is on the right. The mirror-image fold gives Q, which is included as a labelled distractor. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
